svg.title: Fig. 134(a) — The involutes of a curve are parallel curves
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 134(a), page 135. Section: involutes.

g.data-text: The evolute: any curve, drawn heavy. Its tangents will be the stretched string.
Draw the tangents to the evolute at a series of points, here at equal steps of the turning angle. Each one is a position of the straight part of the string.

Fix the end of the string at K, a point of the evolute. On every tangent lay off, from the point of tangency, the length of the arc of the evolute from there to K (the arc is rectified by stepping it off in short chords). These points belong to the first involute.
Lengthen the string by a fixed amount: lay the same extra length beyond the first points on every tangent. This gives the second involute.
And once more, with a further extra length: the third involute.
Draw the three involutes through their points. Every tangent of the evolute cuts all of them at right angles and the same distance apart, so the involutes are parallel to each other.
